prerequisites: The student has relevant technical knowledge regarding programming languages, scripting, operating systems, virtualization, and networks (depending on the track app development or Systems&ICT).

learning_outcomes.text: The student performs a thorough analysis of a complex problem, defines, in consultation with the other team members, the tasks to be performed.
The student divides the defined tasks in consultation with the other team members, creates a plan and adjusts the plan during the project.

The student realizes a part of the total project and his/her realization is representative of the theoretical and practical knowledge gained in the program, supplemented with research where necessary.
The student will report weekly on progress, both verbally and in writing, and adjust the planning where necessary to achieve the set goals.
The student will demonstrate 'ownership': when a problem occurs and is identified, he/she will take the necessary responsibility to ensure that the problem is addressed and solved.

syllabus_topics: From statement of requirements to detailed backlog of tasks
Realization of a multi-disciplinary project in a team context

assessment_methods.method: Practice Enterprise (lab) total team score for realized project
Individual contribution to the total team score (based on reporting, scrum storypoints, ownership, active participation in final presentation)

assessment_rules: The assessment is based on the communicated Practice Enterprise 2 assessment framework: Practice Enterprise (theory) accounts for 20% and Practice Enterprise (lab) accounts for 80%. The theory is assessed based on the evaluation of the associated deliverables (individual). For the realization, a total score for the entire team is calculated, evaluated on analysis, functionality, testing, documentation, and demonstration. Each team member receives a part of that score based on their individual contribution, determined by reporting, percentage of realized scrum storypoints, ownership, and active participation in the final presentation. There is no second exam opportunity for this project.
